utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. And good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please stand and read aloud the affirmation that is given to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Now Mr. Apostolski has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Blagoja Markovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I start asking questions of the witness, we have prepared a binder containing his report, so if we could distribute those.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Dr. Blagoja Markovski, my name is Antonio Apostolski. We know each other already, but let me officially introduce myself with you. Together with Jasmina Zivkovic, we appear for the Defence of Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Before I start asking you questions, I would like to indicate that, although you and I speak the same language, you should still wait for my questions and your answers, as well, to be interpreted in the language understandable for everyone in the courtroom, so let's be mindful of that and facilitate the work of the interpreters. Could you please tell me your full name for the transcript?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: My name is Blagoja Markovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is everything written in your CV that we find in tab 1 of the binder that you just received a contract description of your academic professional and other performances?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. What is of essential significance.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I won't ask you about your CV. Let me just ask you what was the topic you dealt in your Ph.D. thesis, and what was the issue that you developed therein?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: The topic of my Ph.D. thesis was the possibilities for resolving an internal state crisis in transition circumstances. This is actually the current issue of 2001 in the Republic of Macedonia, but also early than that, in the period, in the region of southeastern Europe, where in parallel with the societal transition, there were also some backwards activities taking place in terms of security situation; and from this aspect, this problem has been developed broadly, but the focus has been placed on the Republic of Macedonia, the situation in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender into evidence 65 ter 2D688; that is, the CV of the Dr. Blagoja Markovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be Exhibit number 2D00100. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the Defence give any materials to you so that you would prepare your report?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you clarify for me how did you arrive at the positions you are presenting in your report?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: With regards to the final conclusions I'm presenting in the report, I used various materials for those, and I could divide those into three groups: The first group are the official documents issued by the organs of Republic of Macedonia; the second group are documents assessments, conclusions developed by the international factor present in the Republic of Macedonia, primarily documents of representatives of the United Nations, OSCE representatives that were present with relatively large numbers in the Republic of Macedonia during the crisis, documents coming from the NATO structures that were also present in the Republic of Macedonia , and with which the organs of the Republic of Macedonia cooperated through the structures of KFOR in Kosovo; and the third type of documents are the documents that representatives of the armed extremists have submitted to the Prosecutor's office or to the investigators. I apologise. Of course, I had my own documents, since I am studying this area for a long time already. I'm analysing it; and as I said, it does not deal with the Republic of Macedonia only but with the broader region. So I had my own set of documents dealing with certain events.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You were a witness to the events in 2001?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of 2001, I was an active military officer, lieutenant-colonel. I was head of the service of the public relations service in the army of the Republic of Macedonia and at the same time spokesperson of the army. So from this aspect, one could say that I have been an eye-witness to the events of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: After you finalised your report, did you introduce any corrections to it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I introduced corrections from two aspects. After my arrival here to The Hague, I had certain consultations with you, and I was indicated that considering the fact that the issues, the mission, the tasks, the structure of the Ministry of Interior has already been discussed to quite a large extent, I was suggested that I should omit the items dealing with the Ministry of Interior; and from this aspect I agreed. So I have omitted them from the report. They are no longer part of the report. Item 422 -- I apologise. Item 34, Law on Internal Affairs, together with paragraphs 91 to 98; item 43, structure and forces of the Ministry of Interior, with paragraphs 150 to 185; and item 525, the role of the Ministry of Interior, including paragraphs 226 to 238. As I said, those paragraphs and these items have been omitted from the report. They're no longer part of the report, and that was done by my consent. The second segment of corrections dealt with a completely different issue; and here, as difficult it is for me, I must admit that this has been done because of a mistake that I had made; namely, in item 422, service in the army, when elaborating on the structure positions and definitions dealing with the army of the Republic of Macedonia, in my report, I had used the Law on Service in the Army; whereas, you indicated that considering the fact that this law, the Law on Service in the Army, has been adopted and entered into force after the events of 2001, this document cannot be of relevance. This is why I withdrew what I planned to say on the basis of the Law on Service in the Army, and introduce corrections with regard to the rule book on service in the army which was a document that was in force in 2001. So from this aspect, item 422 and paragraphs 110, 111, 112, 113, 114, and 115 are now similar in content to what has been presented before but they're now based on a relevant document; and amended and corrected, they now have a new format. At the same time, further in the text of the report, where, again, I was invoking the Law on Service in the Army, I have amended the report. In paragraph 207, instead of the words "pursuant to Article 12 of the Law on Service in the Army," I have used "pursuant to Article 28 on the Law on Defence." So the definition of this paragraph deals with the Law on Defence and not the Law on Service in the Army. The same has been done in the paragraph 208, as well as paragraph 211, where the definition I'm giving about the contents of paragraph 211 pursuant to Article 13 of the Law on Defence, was corrected. What I'm asserting there is actually pursuant to the combat rules applicable in the army of the Republic of Macedonia. Amendment has been introduced to the paragraph 372, where, in line 7, the words "pursuant to Article 12 of the Law on Service in the Army," are replaced to "pursuant to Article 28 of the Law on Defence," and the inverted comas are deleted because this no longer deals with the Law on Service in the army. The final amendment is in paragraph 382. At first and second line, the words "Saso Vekovski" are stricken as is the footnote dealing with the two words. These are all the corrections that have been made to the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I thank you for the exhaustive explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the amended report, together with the amendments, be introduced into evidence; that is, 65 ter 2D729.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the amended report shall be given exhibit number 2D00101, and the amended report be given Exhibit number 2D00101.1. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Markovski, I wouldn't like to repeat in my questions what has been already been stated in your report, so I will just ask you questions in order to explain with greater precision some of the positions taken in your report. In your report, your position disagrees with the notion that, in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001, the events should be defined as classical war or armed conflict. Why is that? Why are you making this assertion?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This indeed is my definition. I disagree that the events of 2001 should be defined as classic war or classic armed conflict as a synonym in terms of contents of a war, and this is due to several reasons and due to the conclusions that I arrived at when analysing the events from a scientific aspect. Let me try to do this in brief; although, I believe that simplification of some complex processes as war and peace might lead to certain misunderstanding, but let me try briefly through several sentences to explain my position. For instance, let's define war and peace as two polar extremes: Peace would be the one, and war would the other. It would be very good if we would have a possibility as you lawyers have the scales of justice, and then weigh the things towards one or the other side, and say, "Okay, this side prevails so it is peace"; or put some additional weights on the side of war, and say, "Yes, this looks more like a war." Such black and white image would give us an opportunity to react very swiftly and to define very quickly any situation that belongs to the type of peace or type of war. However, I'm not sure there is a possibility at all to give a definition, that we have an absolute peace or that, on the other hand, we could speak about an extreme of war. So between these two polar opposite, war and peace, there are a number of societal processes taking place. These processes do not follow a straight line. They are sinusoidal. So in the realm of peace, there are both positive and negative societal processes, but also there are positive and negative processes, also I'm saying conditionally speaking, on the side of what is war. For instance, on the side of the peace, from an external viewpoint, we could have various border disputes; minority problems, such as fostering or care for minorities coming from the same ethnic affiliation; also economic pressures; fight for raw materials; also asymmetrical threats, like terrorism, organised crime, which could have the aim of achieving a short-term, but also a long-term, position of interest. In the internal plane, and following the same reasoning, there are economic, societal, minority problems, internal crime. And, of course, in the internal plane, we also have the threats of asymmetrical nature. This could all bring about a crisis in any society, in a given point of time. If it is caused by internal factors, it could be military political; and if it is caused by internal factors, it could be then internally political. The military political crisis usually has the aim of achieving short-term or long-term objectives. The internally political has the aim of achieving various partial interests; economic, social, political, separatist, and various other interests. Somewhere in this conglomerate of social processes, on the side leading to negative elements or leaning towards war, we have the military conflict or armed conflict which could have a low, medium, or high intensity. The basic feature of armed conflict of a how intensity is that we have manifestations of violence. Sometimes, we have demonstrated opened armed violence in terms of incidents, and I'm primarily referring to armed incidents; exchange of fire, activity of terrorist organisations and individuals, as well as activity of the organised internal crime. And at the end we have the war, which, as I said, from what is known thus far in the science, that this is the extension of the political aims achieved through military means, could be or could serve from today's viewpoint as basis to review the issues of war, but without having full merit as definition that would help us define all forms of use of violence, especially at this moment the typical threats such as the asymmetrical actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Before I start my next question, I would kindly ask you to speak a bit slower so that the interpreters could interpret you better.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I will try that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So what would be the application of this to the Macedonian case, regarding which you assert in paragraph 11 that it has been an internal state crisis which was a result of the terrorist and separatist tendencies and activities, supported by the armed individuals, and with the involvement of armed individuals from a neighbouring country in circumstances of sharp economic, social, and internally political difficulties in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Let me go back to the origin of crisis, in general. As I mentioned before, there is really great difficulties in defining ideal state or ideal peace in today's time. But let's suppose that society starts with a state of stability. This state could be disrupted if, in the society, and it happens very often, there are certain problems that I discussed in my previous discussion; economic, societal, minority related, asymmetrical threats related, et cetera. And if the state, through its bodies - in today's time in democratic states, in modern states, we have primarily the crisis management system - so the state, with its bodies, fails to undertake prevention measures in a timely fashion, this problem will grow into a dispute. The dispute also, if no timely measures are taken, can escalate, and its escalation then grows into a crisis. The crisis, in itself and by itself, contains three stages, if we may say so. The first one is the emergence as the mildest form or the first stage in the crisis itself, The second one is the escalation, and the third one is the resolution or the resolving or the deescalation. In the initial, introductory stage, in the emergence of the crisis, we could have various factor, various risk factors, which could be of -- which could be open in type or often undercover nature. This is why the prevention organs, when dealing with the crisis, should without delay assess all the risks and threats present in the society or in a country. The escalation of the crisis is defined and characterised by an open inception of problems, seed of problems, destablisation, or disputes. We have already various contradictions such as still unarmed violence. We have situations and state of confrontations between the entities in a society, regardless of whether these are political entities or other interest groups or self-organised individuals and groups. The confrontation starts which then means non-adherence to the norms and laws of the state, also intimidation. We have open threats, ultimatums, and even armed incidents and use of forms of violence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can I interrupt here, to be more precise about the Macedonian case.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: There was no need to interrupt, because I was going to continue right now. This is something that I had to say because the Republic of Macedonia, back in 2001, facing all these risks and threats that I have mentioned so far, and lacking appropriate system for prevention, which would be established and legally regulated was lagging behind all these events. At the moment, when the crisis could have grown into a military armed conflict of a low, medium, and higher intensity, with the assistance of international factor, most of all the international community and the structures of NATO and the OSCE, it asked for assistance. And the crisis at that particular moment, immediately before it escalated in the third stage of deescalation and dealing with the crisis, the result of that being the fact that in the Republic of Macedonia, there was no bloodshed of the type as we could see in the other regions on the Balkans and south-east Europe. And for these reasons, the Republic of Macedonia, in a much simpler way, started the post-crisis period which provided the opportunity for further development.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If I understood you well, the crisis was stopped by the international factor before it escalated in war.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Not by the international factor but jointly the international factor; that is to say, the Republic of Macedonia with the assistance of the international factor, and this was an assistance that was really necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you for the comprehensive answer. Throughout your report, you are discussing armed extremist groups of ethnic Albanians. Is there a lack of -- is there a difference between your definition and the name given to these armed groups?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: It is true that throughout the crisis these armed groups, back in 2001, were named or called and given different definitions, amongst which the most common once were terrorists, armed extremists, adventurists, and many others, not to mention them all, all the definitions that could portray the real situation of the activities of these groups are concerned. It is my personal opinion after all the analysis that I have carried out, and to a great extent I was helped by the need to analyse all these events for my Ph.D. thesis, I came to the conclusion that we are discussing after all about armed extremists from the Albanian ethnic origin in the Republic of Macedonia which, contrary to the law, and the opportunities in the Republic of Macedonia, took arms illegally, and using the force of the arms tried to achieve certain political goals. Their type of action in the majority of the cases was according to the generally scientifically accepted terminology of terrorism. However, they did not perform terrorist acts on a daily basis. For instance, throughout the month of April in the Republic of Macedonia, the situation was more or less relatively without armed incidents or provocations. This means that I would call these armed extremist groups, but I am not negating the method of their activity as terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer. Going further, in paragraph 54 in your report, you state the following: "The goal of the armed Albanian extremists in the Republic of Macedonia was to achieve their political ambitions through gaining territory and illegally getting the power by holding and maintaining constant tension that will gradually expand to the wider border area along the northern border." How did you come to this conclusion regarding the goals of the armed Albanian extremists?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: One has to bear in mind that the events, back in 2001, in the Republic of Macedonia were happening in a situation when, regardless of the way how we qualify it, it was a situation of democraticisation of the society in the Republic of Macedonia. This would mean that Macedonia was entering the process of its democraticisation to a great extent. The parliamentary democracy was in force in Macedonia at that time, which means that the citizens, in a multi-party general election, they would elect their representatives in the parliament, and they had the opportunity to be represented by the MPs in the Macedonian parliament. During this period, we had 25 Members of Parliament of the Albanian ethnic origin in the Macedonian parliament; that is to say, members of parliament who belong to the political parties who were of the mainly Albanian ethnic origin. We also had ten or so additional Members of Parliament who belonged to the other minority communities. According to the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia, in the Republic of Macedonia, and according to the rules of procedure, the rule book of the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia, democracy in the Republic of Macedonia more or less developed; or at the beginning of its development, allowed for all disputes and questionable issues to be resolved through dialogue; that is to say, in a democratic manner. The armed Albanian extremists, it was obvious that their goal was not for the problems that objectively existed in the Republic of Macedonia, to resolve them in a democratic manner through the institutions of the system; but with the manifestation of their activities, they were trying to create a certain situation, state where they would be able to control one portion of the territory of the Republic of Macedonia, and with additional attempts to establish their own political power on this territory. That is why one cannot discuss any fights for rights of any of the minority groups in the Republic of Macedonia, the Albanian one included, because these activities and requests of theirs were not supported by any other minority or ethnic community, as we would call them later on. And the methodology itself of what they did pointed out that there is a major discrepancy between what they present as a goal for the manifestation of their armed violence and what they really practiced in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Going further, in paragraph 55, you state the following: "The crisis intensified and grew into armed provocations and incidents at the beginning of the first half of February 2001." Then you continue, saying that: "However, the preparations and the creation of the crisis originates from earlier," and you said that this happened with act of independence of the Republic of Macedonia. As a confirmation of this, you refer to the occurrence of paramilitary units in the Republic of Macedonia, in order to establish a quasi-state situation and bringing down the constitution. Who is the one who established this paramilitary formations? Do you remember his? Can you explain this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. We are talking about the beginning of the 1990s, or one year or two years after the independence of the Republic of Macedonia, when a single group comprised of members of the Albanian ethnic community in the Republic of Macedonia. At that time in accordance with the definition of the constitution, members of the Albanian minority in the Republic of Macedonia tried to establish paramilitary formations, with a final goal by using violence to implement their political goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you remember about something in relation to the paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Maybe my colleague could explain what the relevance is of events in Macedonia in the early 1990s to the events in 2001 that are the subject of this trial, because the Prosecution is having trouble seeing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the expert is explaining the genesis of the crisis that contributed for the start of the crisis in 2001, and he is locating when it started and how it developed later on; and, therefore, I believe that this is also relevant in order to corroborate the explanation by Dr. Markovski with respect to the development and genesis of the crisis as a result of the events of 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is your case, then, is it, Mr. Apostolski, that the events of 2001 had their beginnings virtually ten years earlier?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown what is 65 ter 2D538, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Before you see the document on the screen, are you familiar with the incident or the case with the paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How is it familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: I am familiar with it because the appropriate bodies in the Republic of Macedonia detected this case in the stage when it was not fully developed; that is to say, it did not provide for the establishment of a crisis situation; however, there was a situation of established paramilitary structures. It is also familiar to me, maybe I cannot remember precisely, but I believe it was back in 1994 or 1995, in this respect, there was a court case in the Republic of Macedonia, and the leaders of these activities were sentenced by the Macedonian courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you remember any particular individuals of this court process?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I remember almost all individuals who participated in the court proceedings. Let me just mention a couple of them. The first one, Mithat Emini, I remember him well because we come from the same place. We have been born and we use live in the same place. And the second person is Haskaj. He was an assistant in the Ministry of Defence at the same time period when I was working at the ministry. His name is Husein Haskaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown what is 65 ter 2D538, please. We don't have the document on our screens. Very well, we see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see, in front of you, there is a judgement?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this judgement the one that you referred to earlier? It says the district court in Skopje as a second instance criminal court.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the verdict, the judgment that I referred to earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It says the appeals of the accused, Mithat Emini, and all the others, and then the individuals are listed. Then it says these are partly upheld; and, furthermore, you can read that the decision, the judgment of the district court, Skopje Court II in Skopje, shall be changed only with respect to the sentence. Do you see this at the very bottom of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And one can read the sentences, the reversal of the judgment. And at the very bottom, it says that, as far as the rest of the judgment, it is being upheld, confirmed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I can see it, and this is what I already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show page number 14 of the document. Can we scroll to the bottom of the page, please. At the very bottom, if you can see, in the English version, please, the very same page. The following page in English, please. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see in the Macedonian version the sentence starting: "On the 6th of July 1995." This is the seventh row from below on the Macedonian page?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It says: "On the 6th of July, 1993, from the defendant, Husein Haskaj, there was a request sent for the creation of a special unit in the village of Ljuboten; and during November 1993, there was a -- weapons have been confiscated that were presented as evidence. All this, in the opinion of the court, points to the continue unit of the activities undertaken between October 1991 and November 1993." Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document is a subject of a motion for the bar table; but bearing in mind that the expert is mentioning it in his report, the existence of the paramilitary formation, and he recognised these documents. I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Without troubling you, Mr. Saxon, we would not be prepared at this moment to receive this document, Mr. Apostolski, and will deal with it in the course of dealing with the motion that is presently before the Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, and that is why I informed you that is a subject of a motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Going further, in your report where you -- when you were discussing the role of the parliament and the parliamentary committee on security and defence in item 191 of your report, you say the following: "Pursuant to Article 124 of the constitution, a war situation is when there is a direct danger of attack on the Republic or when the Republic has been attacked or was war has been declared?" I would like to ask you whether a state of war has been declared in the Republic of Macedonia back in 2001?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Back in 2001, a war of -- a state of war was not declared.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: According to your professional opinion as a military expert, what was the reason for not declaring state of war?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: There were opinions within certain political circles and clearly presented positions that the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia can be dealt with and resolved only by introducing state of war. But also there was a large number of people in the political entities and the state leadership that the conditions that were to be seen in the Republic of Macedonia at that time cannot be qualified as being that complex in order to declare a state of war. So this is confirmed also by Article 124, because, in order to declare a state of war, in accordance with this particular Article in the Republic of Macedonia, there have to be present three conditions. Three conditions have to be satisfied. The first condition is that an immediate danger should -- imminent danger should be posed to the Republic of Macedonia, and this was not the case because none of the situations, no cross-section of the process could have not been defined as imminent military danger that the Republic of Macedonia was faced with. This would mean attack coming from any of the neighbouring countries. The second condition, to declare state of war, would be if the Republic of Macedonia is under attack. And according to the definition of all the events, it was not attacked by any of the neighbouring countries, military alliance, or any other international military structure. And the third condition, another country should declare war to Republic of Macedonia, but it is a fact that, in 2001, nobody declared war to the Republic of Macedonia. Accordingly, and according to my positions, it is justified that there was no state of war declared in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Apart from the parliament, was there any other state authority that could make a decision for declaring a state of war?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. According to the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia, a state of war can be declared by the president of the Republic of Macedonia, who, in the same time, is the supreme commander of the armed forces, according to the Law on Defence. But also another prerequisite must be met in this case, and that prerequisite being for a president to declare a state of war, there must be a state or a situation when the parliament cannot convene. Before the crisis and during the crisis, as well as in the post-crisis period, the parliament was in a permanent session. So the president, in fact, could not exercise his right; although - I don't know how important that may be for this Chamber - I would like to say that the position or the stance of the president coincided with the stances of all others who thought that, in Macedonia, there shouldn't be a state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Dr. Markovski, in item 239 from your report - that is chapter 6 under the headline appearance of armed Albanian extremists - you define the armed forces or the army in general, and you state: "According to the international military law, according to The Hague rule-book for war law from 1997, and the Geneva Conventions for protection of war victims of 1949, armed forces are defined as land, navy, and air forces, as well as all other armed formations (police units, units of Territorial Defence, factory protection or industrial protection, guards, national guards), and all other voluntary armed forces that, according to the internal regulations of a country, have their insignias, regardless of their size or specialty." Furthermore, you state: "Parts of the armed forces are considered to be units of the organised resistant movement which belong to a war party, regardless of the fact whether they conduct war on their own or in other countries or occupied territory, under the condition that their military members are organised (to be headed by a person that is responsible for his subordinates), then that they have a recognition mark that can be visual as a certain distance, that they openly carry weapons. And another condition is to follow the rules of war law when conducting war." Could you tell me, in reference to what I just read, whether the territory groups of the so-called NLA could be defined as armed forces; that is, an army?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: If we see item 1 of this paragraph 239, we cannot speak about armed forces in the sense that you are putting to me as a question. The doubt, whether these armed forces or armed groups or armed extremist groups, could be defined as armed forces or an army; and, obviously, we must have in mind the last sentence reading that parts of armed forces are also conceded units of organised armed resistance. However, very soon this doubt will be eliminated, because even in this case, there are several preconditions that must be met in order to define one armed formation as armed forces or an army. Let me start with the last condition, and then I will go to the first one. First of all, whenever we have combat activities, they must obey or abide by the war laws. I wouldn't like to reiterate, because in the report, I elaborate all terrorist acts to a great extent, all acts of other types of violence against civilian population in the Republic of Macedonia, the expelling of the population and detaining civilian population, and so on and so forth, which does not give us the right to say that they actually abided by the war law. The second precondition that is stated here is to carry weapons openly. Absolutely, in no case, these extremist armed groups did not carry weapons openly. On the contrary, following the logic, hit and run, they would use their weapons, then they would mingle with the civilian population, and then pretended to be normal civilians as anybody else. The third precondition stated here as a second precondition is to have a recognizable mark that could be noticed at a distance. As far as I could understand this precondition, it means that they needed to have uniforms with all the necessary insignias. And in this report, I believe this Honourable Chamber, you can see a series of cases when certain armed prove significances and incidents were carried out; and during them, the perpetrators did not wear uniforms or had parts of the uniforms that were not really uniforms, according to the definitions. And the last that I would like to comment on, and which is given here as the first precondition, their members should be organised and headed by a person that is in charge of his subordinates. In several documents, one can see that these armed extremist groups were headed by Ali Ahmeti. In many other documents, it is claimed that he was the so-called head or leader of these groups, which also gives us the reason to suspect that this condition was not fully fulfilled, having in mind what I just said about previous conditions. It is obviously that we are not talking about -- about armed groups which can be called armed forces or an army; and commensurate to this, they cannot be a party or a side in the events that happened in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: According to your analysis, did the terrorist group NLA have the support of the Albanian ethnic population in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: There are divided opinions about this, whether and to what extent the members of the Albanian ethnic community in Macedonia supported these extremist armed groups. It is a fact that in many documents - and especially I appreciate the fact that these documents were produced by the international factors in the Republic of Macedonia - one can say that when we speak about the Albanian ethnic community in Macedonia, there were three groups of -- three groups that were directly linked to the armed extremist groups. The first group were those that supported; that is, gave support to these armed extremists. The second group are those that were forced or compelled under pressure to support these groups. And the third group are those that were loyal to the Republic of Macedonia and who didn't support the armed groups at all. The documents from this period give the stance of the political factors that belong to the Albanian ethnicity; and in all of their official statements, there was no support to the armed extremist groups whatsoever. On the contrary, they appealed to them to leave the weapons and through democratic manners, and through dialogue, since such possibility in Macedonia existed, to resolve all the existing problems that were objectively present in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What kind of conclusion did you have from your analysis pertaining to the fact whether the terrorist NLA groups have support from the international community?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: I absolutely and responsibly claim that these armed terrorist groups did not have the support of the international factors. I support this with several documents that are stated here in this report; and on this occasion, I would like to remind of the Resolution 1345 of the Security Council of the United Nations, which calls for a peaceful resolution to the problems on the territory of former Yugoslavia. What referred to the situation in Macedonia, these extremist groups are called terrorists or, to be more precise, defines or qualifies their activities as terrorist activities. Such disagreements were shown by the OSCE and the NATO structures in the Republic of Macedonia, and all of these documents are stated here in this report. Because when I was presenting my conclusions about this issue, I call upon these documents and I state them in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your opinion, and on the basis of your analysis and from the evidence that you had at disposal, did the terrorist group of NLA have any military structure?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: If we take into account the reality, all conclusions and estimates speak that these groups did not have the organisation of a military structure. Allegedly, it could have been heard that the NLA structures were composed of six brigades; but taking into account all factors or standards of an army structure, these brigades could not be brigades in any aspect. They were not brigades judging from their membership or composition, nor could they be brigades according to their weaponry, nor their internal structure, as it was shown by the extremist groups. In Mr. Ostreni's report, he, himself, confirms that these brigades were in the stage of establishment; and that during the crisis period in 2001, they were uncapable of conducting any operation as an organised army. But the so-called brigades worked according to their own independent plans and intentions; and, obviously, this does not speak of an organised structure, let alone an army.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let me follow up. Was there a coordination and continuation of the actions conducted by the terrorist group of NLA?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Although we are speaking about a crisis that lasted several months, some people say it was seven-month crisis. Some say it was nine-month crisis, depending on the beginning or end of the crisis. But this is not really relevant. What is relevant and important is that during this period of seven or nine months, there were no continuous armed provocations or incidents. I would just like to remind that the whole month of April was really quiet. There were no armed incidents or armed provocations of a larger scale. On the other hand, I never came across a document which would speak of any planned organised action by these so-called organised brigades, especially not -- no document about their co-action or documents about any combat activities. As I said previously, Mr. Ostreni confirmed that himself. So we are not talking about planned combat activities, we are not talking about joint activities or cooperation between the so-called NLA structures or the self-proclaimed brigades, and certainly we cannot speak of combat activities that were conducted in a planned pattern and in -- following certain continuity.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Looking at the documents, Dr. Markovski, did you find anything that spoke about NLA having headquarters --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "General Staff," instead of "headquarters."

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: The documents that I analysed and documents that belonged to the members or the structures of the armed extremist groups of the different ethnicity in the Republic of Macedonia, it was mentioned that, allegedly, there was a General Staff. This structure, in the public, released several press releases, mainly following some activities for which responsibility was claimed by them, and they presented these press releases as released from the so-called General Staff of the NLA. However, there was a serious problem here, in respect of the continuity or the establishment of that General Staff and the continuity of its role and its activities. From the analysis of the documents of the international factor, as well as the documents of these extremist groups, it is -- it can be concluded that the General Staff existed in 2000 and even in 2001, while other documents speak that the chief of the General Staff was Mr. Gzim Ostreni. However, there are documents that state that in this period, Mr. Ostreni held a very high position within the protective corps of Kosovo. And the documents are pretty precise in this respect, saying that due to the disrespect of the work procedures within the Kosovo Protection Corps, on the 14th of April, he was dismissed from duty, or was replaced. And the so-called General Staff of these extremist armed groups in the Republic of Macedonia are manned with this person after he was dismissed from the Kosovo Protection Corps; that is, after the 14th of April. This fact is confirmed with the personal statements given by Mr. Ostreni, who really said that he didn't know how the General Staff of the so-called NLA was established, nor did he know where the General Staff was located until his arrival. He also said that he was not familiar with the activities of the so-called NLA before his arrival; or at least whenever he was asked about it, he always disassociated himself from what could be qualified as terrorist groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at line -- beginning at line 9 page 27 of the transcript, the witness describes "documents that state that in this period, Mr. Ostreni held a very high position within the protective corps of Kosovo. And the documents are pretty precise in this respect, saying that due to the disrespect of the work procedures within the Kosovo Protection Corps, on the 14th of April, he was dismissed from duty or was replaced." I could be wrong, Your Honour, but I don't believe that -- well, first of all, this is a fairly important matter because it goes to the credibility of an important Prosecution witness. I don't believe that such documents or such facts are referred to in the expert report of the witness. And I would be grateful if perhaps my colleague, at some point before the end of cross-examination, could provide the Prosecution with such documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Apostolski, you can look at that over the break. We have now reached the time for the first break and will resume at five past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. With regards to the issue that my colleague from the Prosecutor's office raised, I will leave that question for his cross-examination of Mr. Markovski, since perhaps -- since Dr. Markovski has worked for a longer career in the army and he might have information so I believe that my learned friend will be able to deal with that issue during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the problem that the Prosecution sees is that the witness shortly before the first break referred to documents that he relied on to make the point that he made, and it may very well be difficult for the Prosecution to deal with this matter in cross-examination without knowing what those documents are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We appreciate that at the moment, Mr. Saxon, Mr. Apostolski, the proposition asserted by the witness appears to be entirely unsupported. So, in the absence of identified support, that will be its status. If there is support for the proposition which emerges in the course of the evidence, if the Prosecution is embarrassed by a failure of early notice of that support, we will deal with that matter. Thank you, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Markovski, do you remember before the break we discussed the organisational structure of the so-called group NLA?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your expert report, you have dealt with many documents related to the organisational structure of the NLA that were submitted by the so-called group, NLA. Can we agree with this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. These are documents coming from representatives of the extremist armed groups in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Since you have analysed these well in your report, each of those documents individually, could we have a general conclusion about those documents? Could you give us that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I have analysed them individually, and I drew the conclusions in my report. What is common for all these documents that were offered and on the basis of which I ran the analysis of the contents of the documents, the conclusion is that those are not documents of the armed Albanian extremists in the Republic of Macedonia. Without repeating what I said in the report, I have indicated there the reasons, the basis for such conclusion, since it is a nonsense to accept documents like those, if in a given document the need to liberate Kosovo is discussed, if in another document the need to link with the structures at Kosovo is discussed, if in a third document the need to act in coordination with the activities of the Kosovo Guard, Guardist Brigade, I apologise, if in a document it is even mentioned that the drivers in the brigade need to have their vehicles prepared to serve the needs of the members of the Kosovo Guard. So it is obvious that the purpose, the intention of the drafter of this document, is to represent the so-called NLA as an organised structure, a military structure, whereby the drafter of the documents has availed themselves of the opportunity of having such documents previously drafted by some other formation, those documents being in the same language and script used by the Macedonians of Albanian ethnicity, and these documents are then represented as documents of the so-called NLA. I am really specifically elaborating on each of these documents in my report. If there is a need we can discuss my conclusions on this basis, but I believe that they are presented very clearly and I uphold the position that these documents that were tendered into evidence in order to corroborate the notion of the so-called NLA being organised are actually not their documents. The so-called NLA is not an organised structure, and I believe that this could not be accepted as their document. And the fact that other structures documents are submitted in support and in order to justify the existence and the activities of the so-called NLA must be condemned.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your report, item 279, when mentioning Ali Ahmeti, next to his name in quotation marks you say "commander-in-chief and "political representative." Why are you using those quotation marks?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: In many documents, not coming from Macedonian sources but international as well, when mentioning Mr. Ali Ahmeti and his position, his office within the armed extremist Albanian groups in 2001 in the Republic of Macedonia, the so-called political ideologist notion is mentioned or the so-called representative of the armed Albanian extremists, and from this aspect we should accept such definition that I have used. However, I have in mind when speaking about Ali Ahmeti as a supreme commander and the "political representative," so have I in mind the fact also that I haven't encountered any documents and I really made efforts to find any such documents that Mr. Ali Ahmeti was indeed the leader of the so-called NLA. This would presuppose him being elected by those that he represents. In this case, because there is no such document, he could be a self-appointed and therefore so-called leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Dr. Markovski, in your expert knowledge and experience, which is the lowest level of military organisation that should have its own archives, records of their activities?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: It is customary in any army across the world, and so also in the Balkan region and specifically in the Republic of Macedonia, that the lowest level of organisation is the independent platoon within the structure of the army organisation, and after it, company, battalion, brigade, et cetera. So the lowest level where records should be kept about all the activities that a military unit has conducted is the platoon, or, I apologise, the independent platoon, as the first and basic unit where all the planned and executed activities must be recorded. Just as an example, in the Macedonian army in the period that we're discussing, we have had several such independent platoons, so even within those units that were deployed in combatting the threats coming from the armed extremist groups to infiltrate larger cities and urban environments.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Within the documents you researched, did you find any archive documents from any of the units or structures of the so-called NLA?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. And, actually, in the documents that I had the opportunity to analyse, there is a notion of an imaginary battalion and imaginary brigade, so this is a document about an organisation and formation, a structure of a battalion and a brigade unnamed once without numbers, without identification number, which means that such document filed with anyone or submitted to anyone's review could pertain to any unit within the Balkans. Within the south-eastern Europe region, and even within the global ways in which the armies are organised. So we are not discussing any specific unit here. We are discussing some imaginary units that, following certain patterns, are copied from some other formations and are represented as being their units.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P487, Exhibit P487. We could move back to the previous one. Your Honours, my learned friends from the Prosecutor's office were requested by us to show us the original of the map, and the Prosecutor's office informed us that they have it only in electronic version, because the witness, Gzim Ostreni, has provided them with an electronic version only. So there is no hard copy original map and we never had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, have you seen this map, the one that you see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen it, and I have analysed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in on the upper part of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me what is the analysis that you made with regards to this map?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: First of all, I analysed the drawing of this map, and I do understand the Albanian language a bit, so it should be a directive or it should be a decision to carry out a certain operation. The territories are marked as well as the directions of the activities. Probably we will see the narrative part accompanying this map later so we will be able to comment on that as well, since the image without the text would be superficial and the other way around, so we need to analyse them both.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you analyse the locations that are marked with yellow?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the Defence indicate to you that you should run an analysis, if you are able to, about where the village of Ljuboten is, as well as the village of Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Although this map is obviously of poor quality, but considering my knowledge of the situation, I am able to locate Ljuboten and the markings on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you try and locate the village of Ljuboten here in this map and mark it.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: I would be grateful if you could zoom in a bit further so that I'm able to mark precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in a bit further, in the central part of this map. A bit further, if that's possible. Could we zoom in a bit further, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this sufficient or do you need more?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: I think I am able to mark it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If you could -- yes.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is where Ljuboten should be located. To the west of it, we have Ljubanci and to the south-east of it we have Aracinovo and Matejce is to the east.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you mark it with number 1 next to this red circle.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that my colleague is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry to interrupt. Your Honour, there may be a mistake in the translation, I'm just not sure. At the very end of page -- of page 34 and the beginning of page 35 the witness is quoted as saying that to the south-east of Ljuboten is Aracinovo. I'm just not quite sure if that's what he meant to say or not. I could be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So is it correct, what you stated?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. This is what I stated. Aracinovo is to the south from Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So it is correctly written in the transcript that it was to the south-east.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And if the chief of the so-called General Staff of the NLA, the witness Gzim Ostreni, has asserted in his evidence that the territories under the NLA, of the so-called NLA control are marked in yellow, what would you say, as a military expert, under whose control was Ljuboten, and if the map is accurate.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: If the colour yellow depicts the territories where the armed extremist groups were present, then, according to what is shown in this map here, it turns out that in Aracinovo -- or, I apologise, in Ljuboten there have been armed extremist groups. This is in the territory that is marked in yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit 2D00102. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the next page of Exhibit P487. N003-0063-ET; and the Macedonian version is N003-0063-MF. We see here the Albanian version, but would it be possible to delay the Macedonian and the Albanian version --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Macedonian and English versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I repeat, the Macedonian page is N003-0063-MF. We now see the Macedonian version, but if we can have the English version back on the display. It is fine now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you reviewed this document when preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you comment on it, in brief.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: First of all, I wish to remind that this document originates, or at least this is the date it bears, from 13th of June, 2001. I would like to remind that this is a significant period with regards to the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia, since, on the 8th of June, President Trajkovski tables a plan to resolve the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia primarily through political dialogue. This plan was officially presented by President Trajkovski in the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia, where, in addition to the MPs that made up the parliament, all the other relevant factors in the Republic of Macedonia were present, having in mind both political as well as ethnic and religious representation. This plan was simply accepted, endorsed by the parliament, and already on the 12th of June the government came with an official statement that it not only joins the acceptance of the plan of President Trajkovski to resolve the crisis through dialogue but is even prepared through -- to make it operational through planned measures and activities. As I mentioned, this document of the so-called NLA was issued on the 13th of June, so five days after President Trajkovski's plan was presented and made official and one day after the confirmation that the government is ready to make it operational, to make the plan of President Trajkovski operational. These needs -- or this should give us the idea that regardless of the attempts and efforts that the Macedonian state and political leadership have made to find a solution for the crisis through a political dialogue, Ali Ahmeti has signed on the 13th of June ideas to run operations. So, actually, he did not accept President Trajkovski's plan and his recipe to resolve the crisis is obviously through military activities. However, let me deal now with the analysis of the contents of this idea, to run this operation. I don't want to be misunderstood; however, some commander, if he would come to me to take an exam with this kind of operation, it is not just that he would pass the exam but I would send him back to the first grade to study both tactics and organisation of the military structures. I do apologise for saying this, but I will tell you why it is I do this. First of all, this is not the correct form, nor content for conducting any type of operation. Secondly, everything written here is so unrealistic, impossible to implement, and, indeed, it does not deserve any further attention, and any possible taking of these activities in accordance with these kind of ideas with conducting the operation would only cause a major bloodshed. I will just remind you about a particular segment of this idea for conducting the operation. This is really military lack of literacy, to be able to plan, for instance, that in the second stage by the end of July Kumanovo is going to be taken over and controlled and the roads Kumanovo-Kriva Palanka, Kumanovo-Sveti Nikole, Kumanovo-Skopje will be placed under control. In order to further elaborate this problem, I would like to say the following, that the -- in order to control the roads from Kumanovo to Kriva Palanka and Kumanovo to Sveti Nikole, probably you need troops and equipment far too powerful and much more than what was presented or what was said that is at the disposal of these terrorist extremist groups in Macedonia. And number two, even if they succeed in doing that, the configuration of the terrain is such that they would need at least to establish a military base comparable to Bonstil in Kosovo in order to be able to sustain it and to maintain it under control. The other ideas are similar. I don't know want to go into further detail. From the military point of view this is amateur stuff, and the beginning of any type of implementation of this idea for the conducting of the operation would only cause major catastrophe and huge number of victims but not implementation of the ideas and implementation of the plan itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You mentioned the configuration of the terrain on the road from Kumanovo to Kriva Palanka and from Kumanovo to Sveti Nikola. Can you please explain what kind of configuration it is and why would you mention this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is a terrain which is overhanging on the surrounding area and we are discussing an open space. There are no forests which, on the other hand, would be a very good target to act against those units that might be located on this position from any possible direction in the neighbouring regions. Just in order to remind you, immediately following these cross-roads, especially the cross-roads Kumanovo to Sveti Nikole, there is a terrain which, during the Second World War, the people who were fighting at the location of Stracin, they died, and even today the soil in Stracin is still red from their own blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer to my question. Now let us move to another topic? The Defence of Mr. Johan Tarculovski asked you to provide an expert opinion about the events from 10th to 12th of August, in the village of Ljuboten in 2001. In the documents that you disposed of and reviewed in order to prepare the report about the events in Ljuboten, you are claiming that in the village of Ljuboten there was a structure of an armed group, Albanian armed group provocation and incidents, and this is your summary provided. When drafting your position and report about Ljuboten, you were using many documents coming from different bodies of the security institutions of the Republic of Macedonia, amongst others, documents from the operative centre General Staff G2 within the Ministry of Defence, as well as information of the subordinate units and commanders of the General Staff of the Macedonian army. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you, did the president of the state, being commander-in-chief, get a report from the security structures?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The security structures are obliged to provide regular reports to their supreme commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In what manner does the president receive information?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: There are several ways to inform the supreme commander about the events that are going on and are related to the security, both in peacetime, in normal conditions, but also in conditions of crisis. The regular manner in which the president is being informed about the situation related to the security is through the operative centre of the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, which, during its work and operation of the units for 24 hours they prepare a summary information, and this information, every single day at 8.00 a.m. the next day, is being sent to the commander, that is to say, the supreme commander. In the event that we might be facing an extraordinary event, then the Chief of Staff, after receiving this information and after being informed about the incident, he would inform the president on the very same day when he hears about the event, and the very next morning at 8.00 a.m., this information with a more explanation will be supplied or submitted to the Supreme Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This would mean that the events in Ljuboten on the 10th of August, 2001, where eight soldiers have been killed and a few more injured, the president should have been informed by phone by the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And when would he receive the regular report?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: The regular report, with more information about the incident, he would receive it the very next day at 8.00 a.m. However, the president, being the Supreme Commander, if he is interested to receive this information sooner, he can order the Chief of Staff, together with all the relevant information about a particular event, for the Chief of Staff to come to his cabinet in order to inform him in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: With regards to what I asked you earlier about the materials that you have been using in relation to Ljuboten, on the basis of your opinion provided about the events in Ljuboten, I would like to ask you more specifically the following: Does the president of the state have the opportunity to dispose of the documents that you have used in your report?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I am quite sure that he would dispose of these documents because these documents are very important and they would be a part of the information with which the Supreme Commander would be acquainted.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could Dr. Markovski please be shown what is Exhibit P301.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is a report about a terrorist attack prepared by the command of the 3rd Guardist Battalion, village of Ljubanci, 10th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Amongst others, it speaks of the following: "The unit that was at the Zdravec position replied to the activity of the terrorist in order to provide the opportunity to give help to the victims. At the same time, in coordination with the battalion command, fire was opened with a mortar fire, shells of 120-millimetres and two weapons, B-1, 76 millimetres. "After that the terrorist ceased their action and they withdrew in the action of Sveti Kamen, position 1628, and a smaller group (three to four) in the direction of Ljuboten. Also the latter was noticed by our lateral positions as they entered one of the two abandoned sheepfolds and fire was opened upon them with 15 missiles from the cannon B-1, after which one of the terrorists was noticed as he fled above the sheepfold in the direction of the facility Kuljim, and the sheepfold was destroyed."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the second page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On -- the second page of this document reads as follows: "Two of them at the entry to the village, in the further activities by our unit, four terrorists have been killed, two of them at the entry of the village, one above the drinking fountain above the village Ljuboten, who was accompanied by a horse, and a fourth in the region above the small woods on the road leading into the village with a mule with a load?" Now I would like to ask you whether the president would have this type of information about the events in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: First of all, the operative centre of the General Staff would be provided with this information, then the operative centre of the General Staff would prepare a summary of the most important events, and then they would submit this to the president, i.e., to the Supreme Commander. And if the head of the operative centre believes that besides the prepared summary, the overall content of the information is important, then the whole information can be supplied as an appendix to the report given to the Supreme Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown what is 65 ter 742, ERN N002-4490, N002-4492. Your Honours, this is a document that can be found on the 65 ter list of the Prosecution, and we informed the Prosecution that we were going to use this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see, this is a document, a report about extraordinary incident. On the top one, can read, Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Defence, General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, 1st Guardist Brigade. The reference number is provided and the date is 10th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show to the witness the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: One can see that it was prepared by commander Colonel Blazo Kopacev. It reads, under paragraph 11 on this page, and it provides a short summary of the incident: "Immediately following the explosion on the soldiers and the soldiers who came to their aid, sniper fire has been opened and auto weapons fire from the direction of the slopes at Svinski Kamen and Bel Kamen and a mosque in the village of Ljuboten. Our forces respond with all disposal weaponry on these targets, after which the attackers retreated." Can you please tell me who is Colonel Blazo Kopacev?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: At that time, the commander, Colonel Blazo Kopacev, was the colonel of the Guardist Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this document that the president of the state could have had at his disposal?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, bearing in mind that the document is on the 65 ter list of the Prosecution, the Defence informed the Prosecution that we are going to use this document, and that is why I seek to tender it into evidence, to be placed on our list and to be accepted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 2D00103. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 2D42; page 8 in the Macedonian version and page 7 in the English version. Can we show the first page, first of all, so that the expert can see what type of document it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is a log on the information received on 10th and 11th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: There are several parts in this document. We have the reference number. In the second column, we have the date; the third one, the time; the fourth column, the origin of the document.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Basically, the source of the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Then in the following column, we have the contents of the information; furthermore, who has been informed; the time when the information was provided; and the name of the person who informed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see the eighth page in the Macedonian version and page number 7 in the English version. At the very bottom of the English version, number 13, please, and in the Macedonian version, number 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is information received from G2.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Received on the 10th of August at 1655.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please explain to us what is G2.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. G2 is the intelligence sector within the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It reads here that information has been received.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please turn to the next page in the English version:

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: "Information received that a group of around 100 individuals has to depart from the region of the village of Matejce towards the villages of Ljubanci, Ljuboten, Brodec, and Kodra Fura, with a task to conduct an attack on the points of the defence and security forces. Additionally, intelligence has been received that, allegedly ..." -- we don't really need to read any further. This is the important bit. Did the president of the state, would he have this type of information, this information at his disposal?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Bearing in mind the importance and the significance of this information, it would be part of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a bit difficult to understand the record, as it is now. And just for clarification, could the witness be asked whether he knows whether the president received this specific information or whether this was the kind of information that the president might have received.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let us clarify then. You, as an expert, and a person with a large experience, member of the Ministry of Defence, according to your knowledge, can you please give me an answer, whether the president would have had this type of information at his disposal?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
