utterances.text: I was not just a member of the army during this period, but quite often, and in accordance with the distribution of the tasks, I also had the obligation of chief person of the operative centre on duty on a particular date, for on-duty call for 24 hours. And from my personal experience, but also the knowledge that I have assessing, on the other hand, the importance and significance of this information because it is rather important for the information to the president, I would say that, absolutely, yes, the president would have had this information at his disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this confirm the fact that the president of the state was very well informed about the security situation in the region?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The president was capable and at any time he would have had a realistic picture about the security situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sorry for the interruption again. It just appears to the Prosecution that my colleague is starting to ask leading questions about what could be a very crucial topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that's the case, Mr. Saxon. Mr. Apostolski, could you be much more careful about your questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will be more careful, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let us move to another topic. What would happen if a subordinate officer falsely informed his superior that the president issued him an order to undertake an action?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Any superior at any post, including the chief of the General Staff as the highest military officer in the army, does not have the right to file false reports, because, in doing so, he would violate the military discipline which, at that time, was regulated with the rule book on the service in the army; that is to say, by an act like this, he would severely violate the military discipline. This would, in turn, mean that he would be dismissed or even let go. This is, I believe, pursuant to Article 31 of the rule book on the service in the army, but this can be checked. This is a document that is being discussed in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now specifically about Ljuboten, about the events in Ljuboten. What would happen if the commander of the 3rd Battalion, Mitre Despodov, would inform the Colonel Kopacev, brigade commander, that he spoke to the president and he received an order from the president and if this was untruth?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: In this case, according to the prescribed procedure, the Major Despodov would find himself in a situation where he would be punished; that is to say, he would be denoted of his ranks or he would be relieved from the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: As you said, you had been in the army for a long time. Do you know what happened with Major Mitre Despodov after 2001?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Long after 2001, I still stayed within the Ministry of Defence, and I know very well that then-Major Mitre Despodov was promoted in the rank of lieutenant-colonel and was in charge of the training command in the General Staff of the army of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Blagoja Markovski, for your reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Residovic, do you have any questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Dr. Markovski. Although we met previously, let me introduce myself. My name is Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague, Guenael Mettraux, we are defending Mr. Ljube Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since I'm going to use several documents in the course my examination, we, for the Chamber and for our colleagues from the Prosecution, as well as for the witness, we prepared several binders that we are going to use in questioning this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, I would like to ask you, just like my colleague did, to wait until my question is translated before you reply, so that we go I have the opportunity to the interpreters what I'm asking and what you are replying. Do we understand each other?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 197 and 198 of your report, you speak about the constitutional position of the president of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown the Exhibit P91, Article 79 of the constitutional of the Republic of Macedonia; and in reference with this Article, I'm going to ask you the following questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Markovski, is it that is correct that the Article 79 of the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia establishes that the president of the Republic of Macedonia is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, is it correct -- is my understanding correct if I were to say that under armed forces are considered to be both the army and the police?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, is it correct that in 2001, very often, instead of armed forces, the term security forces was used?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. As a synonym to the armed forces, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Markovski, that this term "security forces" also encompassed the army and the police forces?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And there is also a document that confirms your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You just mentioned a document, and I would like to ask you to look the document of tab 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit 1D313. It is a Law on Special Rights of the Members of the Security Forces. I apologise. That is in tab 17, so it is Exhibit 1D313.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you, you just said a document that says precisely what security forces are. In front of you, you have a law on special rights of members of the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia and the members of their families. Did you have this law in mind when you said that there was a document that sets precisely who composes security forces?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. That is exactly the law that I had in mind, together with its Article 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Dr. Markovski, that this term, "security forces, "as a synonym for the armed forces, was used mainly because the Law on Defence reduced the constitutional provisions and said that armed forces are only the forces of the army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. In the previous law of 1995, it was defined that the president was the Supreme Commander of the armed forces. And with the new law that was adopted that the second half of the 2001, the word "armed forces" was replaced with "army," which, in fact, did not reduce the rights and responsibilities of the president as the Supreme Commander, but this may be one of the reasons why the decision was made more precise about what were the security forces in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You just explained about the new Law on Defence. Could you tell me if the constitution, in any way, restricted the authority of the president as the Supreme Commander?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. The constitution does not limit these rights with any of the provisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We saw the Exhibit P91 and Article 79, item 2, which determines that the president of the Republic of Macedonia is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces of Macedonia. In paragraph 3 of the same Article, it is said that the president of the Republic of Macedonia executes his duties and responsibilities within the constitution and the laws. Please tell me, Dr. Markovski, having in mind this provision, do the laws, or any law in particular, can restrict the established constitutional authority of the president of the Republic of Macedonia as the Supreme Commander?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. These laws that you have mentioned, that we are discussing, cannot restrict the constitutional authority of the president; that is, the Supreme Commander of the armed forces. They can only operationalise the provisions and paragraphs within the constitutional of the Republic of Macedonia that pertain to the president.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Dr. Markovski, does this position of the Supreme Commander that is performed by the president of the country is limited to the state of war or state of peace, or the president of the country is always the Supreme Commander of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe that earlier, when responding to the question by Mr. Antonio, I mentioned that the president is a Supreme Commander both during peace and war.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for maybe repeating the question for which you already gave an answer; but responding to the question of my learned colleague, did I understand you well that the authority of the president of war and his role of a Supreme Commander, was it only for the state of war?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, please tell me, having in mind the analysis of the documents that you made and on the basis of your personal and professional experience in 2001, did the president of the state use his authority as the Supreme Commander, although state of war was not declared?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the factual situation, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that he directly derived his authorities from the constitutional provisions?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, and he would emphasise that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit 1D52.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you have it in tab 11. Here we see 1D52, under seal. We have the decision of the president of Macedonia, dated 7th of August, 2001, about the use of the army of the Republic of Macedonia. That is an order. And in the preamble of this order of the president, it is said: "Pursuant to Article 79, item 2 of the constitution of Macedonia, and in accordance to the newly established safety situation, I issue," and so on. End of quotation. Is this one of the documents that confirm your response that the president frequently used his constitutional right to issue orders?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is precisely so. And the president is rather precise in this decision, and he refers to Article 79, item 2 of the constitution which provides him with this right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, when you were analysing the document that you stated in your report, and in accordance with your personal experience, do you know if the president issued orders to the army and the police, and whether the army and the police had the obligation to implement those orders?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The answer would be yes and yes. Yes, he issued orders both to the army and the police; and, at the same time, both army and police were obliged to implement orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask that the witness is shown 1D90, page 1D43 -- 4036 in Macedonian; English version, 1D4038.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, let me ask you, were you familiar --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can turn the document in tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the decision of the minister of the interior affairs to disband the reserve composition of the police?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I did have such document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know what happened with that decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: This decision, upon order of the Supreme Commander, the president, was withdrawn by the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On this page of this document, in the last paragraph after the three asterisks, it said the composition of the reserve structure, and then it is said: "The minister of the internal affairs, at the press conference, said that the members of the reserve composition of the Republic of Macedonia will be demobilised and withdrawn from the check-points around Skopje." When you were responding to my question, did you have in mind, that, in 2001, you were also familiar with the decision written in this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the document in tab 16.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit 1D91, and that is the page 1D41 -- 4042, and the English is it 1D4042.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the end of this document, it is said that: "The police reservists are returning to the check-points and the Ministry of Internal Affairs withdrew the decision for the demobilisation of the police composition, and ordered for remobilisation which will be processed selectively. The remobilisation of the police reserve composition is conducted upon a request of the Supreme Commander of the Macedonian armed forces, Boris Trajkovski, due to the actual security situation in the country." Does the contents of this document correspond to your knowledge, Dr. Markovski, about the decision of the Supreme Commander to withdraw the decision of the minister of internal affairs?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe this would be a convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Ms. Residovic. We will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, the president of the state, as the Supreme Commander, has issued order also for the joint operations, to both the army and the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you to look at the document in tab 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] that is Exhibit 1D58, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is a decision of the president of the Republic of Macedonia dated 4 June 2001, where, in item 1, it is stated: "The army of the Republic of Macedonia and the units of the Ministry of Interior shall prepare and carry out an attack operation in the broader region of Skopska Crna Gora mountain?" Tell me, Dr. Markovski, is my understanding correct, if I were to say that this is a direct order of the Supreme Commander to the units of the Ministry of Interior as well?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Since the Supreme Commander, by its decision, orders that the army of the Republic of Macedonia and the units of the Ministry of Interior should prepare and carry out the aforementioned operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of this decision, it is stated: "Preparation of the units should begin immediately, and the operation should start upon a decision of the head of the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia." Is it correct, Dr. Markovski, that president of the state, as the Supreme Commander, also brought the decision who would be the immediate head of the operation?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the reading of this paragraph, and it is also noted that the operationalisation and the preparations will be done upon an order of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With -- in one part of your expert report, point 4.2, you spoke about the army of the Republic of Macedonia and its organisational structure, service, recruiting, et cetera. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you agree with me, Mr. Markovski, if I were to say that no other state structure in the Republic of Macedonia works in the same way as the army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is an inherent feature of the Republic of Macedonia, of the army of the Republic of Macedonia to act like this. So no other structure works like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the main feature is commanding in the army of the Republic of Macedonia, while in the other state structure we have management?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. In the army the orders are carried out based on principle of command, while in the other structures we have management. They are all synonyms in Macedonian, "upravuranjge," "rakovodenje," "menadzment."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right, Dr. Markovski, if I say that the basic principles upon which the army of the Republic of Macedonia is founded, and which are known to most of modern continental armies, were known in the JNA as well and remained applicable in the army of the Republic of Macedonia in 2001?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Those are internationally recognised and I would say verified principles of command, and they are applicable in the Republic of Macedonia. That would mean in the army of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, is one of these principles the unity of the command when deploying forces and means?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: That is one of the main principles, without which a structure like this could not be operational, could not function.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that this principle of unity of command does not tolerate possibility of dual command within a single combat operation?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: You're absolutely right. In one combat operation, there could be -- there could not be two commanders. The operation is led by a single commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Dr. Markovski, that the next main principle, upon which the army of the Republic of Macedonia was founded, was the principle of singleness of command?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And would it be correct if I stated that this main principle excluded any possibility for other type of command, than with a single head, in a joint combat operations and activities carried out during that time?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. The operation must presuppose a single commander. This is the principle of singleness of command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that the next basic principle in the army of the Republic of Macedonia was the obligation to carry out the orders and decisions of the superior officers? That would mean full subordination in the carrying out of decisions and orders.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: That is a principle and also a legal obligation binding any military officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean, Dr. Markovski, that it is precisely because of the principles upon which the army of the Republic of Macedonia is established, that any use of other forces carrying arms - police, for instance - would require that, in a joint operation or action, the police is necessarily placed under the command of the officers of the army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Starting from these principles, and I hope we clarified them, you are completely right. This is how things must be.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraphs 86, 87 of your expert report, you spoke about the new Law on Defence being adopted, and it entered into force on the 8th of June, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Dr. Markovski, that some provisions of this law were identical to the provisions of the old law. You mentioned Article 1 and some other Articles at the beginning. So the new law was immediately applicable with regards to those provisions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: The new law followed the development processes in the defence sector in the Republic of Macedonia, and that was the reason for its adoption. I am not completely clear what your question is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that some provisions of the law that were either fully identical to the ones in the previous law or have clearly regulated a given situation were applicable immediately? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Some were; some were not. And in the final provisions of the law, it is indicated which among the new positions or new provisions in the law are immediately applicable and which are delayed for a certain period of time, because in order to apply them, the adoption of secondary legislation was necessary. So this is how it depended, which of the secondary legislation items would be adopted when, in order to be able to promote, if I may say so, some of the new provisions in the law; and the final provisions of the law make it precise which are those new provisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You already answered the next question that I was about to ask. Is it true that the final and provisional clauses of the new law established that the new law is applicable until the regulation is adopted which is necessary to make the new provisions of the law, those that you indicated, applicable?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Not only I wish to confirm this; but even beyond, some of the provisions are still not in force -- provisions of the new law are still not in force because secondary legislation was not adopted to date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this avoided a legal gap, so all organs were able to act, applying either provisions of the new law or provisions of the old law. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, you're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering the position of the president of the Republic, tell me, is it correct that his position of the Supreme Commander towards the armed forces, including both the army and the police, remained completely identical throughout 2001, identical to what has been stipulated in the old law?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 4.2.3 -- actually, in this part, paragraph 116, et cetera, you spoke about calling up the reserve forces to join the army of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this, Dr. Markovski, I will kindly ask you to clarify a given situation, and it is true that it has been discussed at length before this Chamber. Namely, is it correct that all citizens of the Republic of Macedonia of full age, after serving their conscription military service, are given a place in the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Every citizen of the Republic of Macedonia who serves their conscription military service has the duty, within 24 hours from the discharge from the army after the conscription period ends, has the duty to report to the unit of the Ministry of Defence --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ministry of?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: I apologise. Ministry of Defence where the person will be deployed within a unit of the reserve forces, where they will perform if there is need for that; in other words, they are given a military deployment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, as you said, the military deployment for every citizen of the Republic of Macedonia of full age is kept at records in the Ministry of Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is a special unit that deals exclusively with those issues within the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And for each of the citizens, there is the military deployment or deployment for every single individual in case where a call-up of the reserve forces is needed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the main functions of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that no citizen of the Republic of Macedonia of full age could have two military deployment posts at the same time, to be simultaneously in the tank unit and infantry, or to be simultaneously in the infantry or in the police reserve. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. Every citizen who has served their conscription service can have a single deployment within a single unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, for a citizen of full age to be transferred, for instance, from the army of the Republic of Macedonia into the police of the Republic of Macedonia, it would be necessary to, first, change the military deployment as recorded in the Ministry of Defence, is that correct, if they were not originally deployed to serve in the police, of course?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, no citizen of full age can have two military deployments at the same time. This means that the reservist, the citizen of the Republic of Macedonia of full ages, could not have simultaneously military deployment within an army unit and within a police unit. That is impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can I conclude from your answer, Dr. Markovski, that if someone actually came to a police station that, without having changed their military deployment records, this very fact that the person has come to a police station would not make him a police reservist?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: It is absolutely impossible, because for such transformation, if I may call it so, a consent or agreement must be given by a head of the unit of the Ministry of Defence dealing with the deployment of the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, Dr. Markovski, if someone failed to meet the requirements for the unit or for the structure where the military deployment was originally planned, what would happen to such person?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: You raise as dilemma, what if they failed to meet the requirements, but I would broaden this. It might be due to health reason that they are unable to serve on that post any longer, then they would be given another deployment post, depending on the professional and vocational training, also military training and compatibility to perform tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that this other deployment would decided by the Ministry of Defence, "it" being the civilian body that keeps the records of military reservists?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: It is only the Ministry of Defence, yes, that unit within the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will kindly ask now that the witness is shown the 65 ter document, 1D1295. That is a document in tab 19 in the binder, and the page is 1D2091 and the English 2D0297.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, this is a document of the Ministry of Interior, sector for internal affairs, Skopje, section for defence preparation. The date is 25th of September, 2001, and it is sent to the Ministry of Defence, regional unit for defence, Karpos, Skopje. Subject is notification delivery. "We notified you that the following reserve conscripts are deleted from our register of reserve composition conscripts with approved military disposition in SVR-Skopje, list with code II/3" and then we have a name. Then "list with code II/7," and then there is another name indicated. "We are seconding the above mentioned reserve conscripts to your competence for any deployment within other units within the reserve structures." Tell me, Dr. Markovski, is this the way in which that the section for defence preparations in the Ministry of Internal Affairs has the duty to inform Ministry of Defence in order to remove a person from the list of police reservists if they have originally been included in that list?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, you're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you kindly now look at the document after tab 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 65 ter 1D1296, which is 1D09 -- 0292, and the Macedonian page -- that was the Macedonian page, while the English is 1D0298.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, again, we have a similar document coming from the section for defence preparations within the sector for internal affairs in Skopje, dated 21st of August, 2001. And, again, it is sent to the Ministry of Defence. The subject is notification, delivered. It reads: "We notified you that from the separated files of reserve composition conscripts in your PEO, at the beginning of April 2001, upon a completion of the prescribed procedure by our side enlisted of VES in SVR Skopje by six conscripts altogether was conducted," and the six persons are listed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please can we turn to the second page in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: "We inform you that the remaining nine conscripts for which the files have been set aside upon the conducted checks, it was established that they do not fulfil the prescribe the criteria for the enlistment in VES in SVR Skopje?" Is this also a document that is a collaboration of your claim that any change, regardless if a person is being transferred in the reserve forces of the police or for any other reasons has to be relieved from the police services, it has to be done still within the unit at the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can understand this document, upon request of the Ministry of Interior, the Ministry of Defence has provided these people who were recorded and maintained at the Ministry of Defence; and since they do not satisfy all the criteria, the document does not list which ones - these can be professional criteria as well - the Ministry of Interior is obliged to return their personal fails; that is to say, to inform the Ministry of Defence that these individuals are accepted and the others are being sent back. This means that the continuity continues of the records being maintained at the Ministry of Defence. This is the correct method and confirmation of the fact that no military reservists can have two different deployments, nor they can be lost in the records.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender the following documents, 1D295 and 1D296, first of all, to be included on the list, and then to be accepted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Those two documents --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the first one, 1D1295, and the second one, 1D1296.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you sure that second number is correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 1D1296.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Those two documents will be received, and they will add to the list.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D01295 shall be Exhibit number 1D00350, while 1D01296 shall be Exhibit number 00351. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please repeat it, because it was not fully entered into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D01295 shall be Exhibit number 1D00350, while 65 ter 1D01296 shall be Exhibit 1D00351. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, earlier, we discussed that the president of the Republic, as a Supreme Commander, does not have any restrictions in relation to issuing orders to the military, army, and the police, and the operationalisation of the Joint Command when conducting a joint action. Do you remember us discussing this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, if I were to ask you or suggest that the president of the state, as a Supreme Commander, does not have any legal or constitutional limitations even to manage a combat operation even on his own, would it be true?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Considering the constitution and the laws, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us move to another topic now that you discuss in your own report. You were discussing in details in your report, and that is why I won't be asking about all the activities of the NLA. But what I want to ask you is the following: Is it true that these terrorists groups of the NLA started attacking in June, not just the Tetovo region, but also in the region of Kumanovo and Skopje?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. But it wasn't an organised activity but separate armed incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And some armed forces or groups entered the village of Aracinovo; whereas, other groups started to threat with attacks on the refinery, the airport, and the capital city of the Republic of Macedonia as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that these terrorists sabotage groups used or utilized the mountain Skopska Crna Gora along whose slopes parts of the city are also located, and the whole city is located in the foot of the mountain, in order to link up their groups in the Kumanovo and Tetovo region with Kosovo, and to use these positions on the mountain in order to threaten the capital city? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. You are completely right, because there was no link or possibility for linkage of activities of certain extremist armed groups from the Kumanovo region and their coordination with similar groups coming or originating from the region of Radusa.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 338 in your expert report, you are discussing the adoption or enactments of decisions for the establishment of the command for defence of the city of Skopje. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this decision a result precisely of these threats towards the city of Skopje from the slopes of the mountain of Crna Gora?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Based on the professional assessments that have been conducted within the security structures, I would say that this is precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, can you take a look at the document in tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] this is Exhibit 1D99.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And please tell me whether this is the decision that President Trajkovski made on the 11th of June in order to establish the defence command for the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please take a look now at the document in tab 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] this is Exhibit 1D100.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Dr. Markovski, that the very same day, the president of the Republic, being the Supreme Commander, issued a decision for the mobilisation of the forces, in order to be able to fully implement his decision for the establishment of the defence command for the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is so. However, I would like to offer a clarification, because here, it is being ordered to mobilise the 12th and the 16th Infantry Brigade, the 1st Guardist Brigade, and the 8th Infantry Brigade. At the time when this order has been issued, the 1st Guardist Brigade and the 8th Infantry Brigade, they existed together with their military composition; whereas, the 12th and the 16th Infantry Brigade, as formations of the reserve forces, they only had the command structures, and it was really necessary to mobilised these structures; that is to say, to invite the reserve structures of these units to continue with the activation of these couple of units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please can you take a look now at the document in tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] this is Exhibit 1D81. The page is 1D3042 in the Macedonian version and 1D3048 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document, Dr. Markovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I have it as part of my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the very same day when the president of the Republic issued the order for the establishment of the defence command for the city of Skopje at 1800 hours, the commander of the defence of city of Skopje, General Mitevski, issued the order for the defence for the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this order, in the second paragraph of item number 1, one can read the following: "After encountered failures in the clashes with the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia, in the populated places on the eastern slopes of Skopska Crna Gora, noticeable are the efforts of the terrorists to transfer the action to the region of Skopje and to the facilities of vital importance for the normal life of the population and the operation of the bodies of the state authority. The terrorists control the village of Aracinovo, where they have set up barricades on the roads, and they conduct preparations for the defence of the village. One can register their incursions also in the neighbouring villages." Then it gives the other reasons. My question is whether this order contains the basic reasons for which the decision for the establishment of the defence command has been established or made, about which you provided your own opinion in the report and answered my previous questions. So are these reasons, do they correspond to your own knowledge and conclusions?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. These are the basic reasons for the enactment of the decision and order, as well as this order for the defence of the city of Skopje; and, basically, you read them out loud, so there is no need for me to repeat those.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, can you agree with me that the defence of the capital city is the most significant, if I might say so, defence task of the military and all other armed forces, including the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. This is the basic qualification for the need to defend the capital city of any country, including the Republic of Macedonia, because this is where all the state and other capacities are located.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that, in this type of important tasks, one cannot have more than one order, and the order issued by the commander for the defence of the city of Skopje have to be followed by all other security forces, including the police?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct; otherwise, the situation would be diluted and the final goal would not be achieved.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you take a look at item number 2 of this order by the commander of the defence of the city, the task is being listed. It says: "Task, in joint action with the neighbours and the bodies of the Ministry of Interior and civil defence, to control the access points towards the city of Skopje, to destroy the discovered sabotage and terrorist groups, and hinder the infiltration of sabotage and terrorist groups into the city and the region of the vital facilities an action upon these." First of all, I will ask you, Dr. Markovski, is my understanding of this order correct if I say that this is an order that relates also to the bodies of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: This order relates, besides to the listed units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, to the bodies of the Ministry of Interior, but also units of the civilian defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, is my understanding of this order also correct, if I were to say that the commander of the defence of the city ordered to destroy the discovered sabotage and terrorist groups and to prevent their infiltration in the city?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is clearly mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this task, is it correct that it was -- it would oblige all the entities mentioned in this order?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This all refers to all the entities and bodies listed here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]I will ask now for the second page to be shown, the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Item number 3 reads, "Neighbours." Please, tell me, Dr. Markovski, who these neighbours are?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI
utterances.text: So we have an order for the defence of the city of Skopje, and it is precisely addressed to the entities that are supposed to provide the defence of the city of Skopje. As we already mentioned, these are the army units that are listed here, the bodies of the Ministry of Interior, and civilian defence. All of those, as part of the task, they have their own field of responsibility defined by the constitutional and legal obligations. So, as I mentioned, they have a particular field of responsibility. Immediately besides those, they might have other units of the army or security forces, and they also have their own field of responsibility. So when discussing neighbours, we are talking about the neighbouring unit, the neighbouring bodies of the Ministry of Interior or the civilian defence; that is to say, the neighbouring field or zone of responsibility. And just to mention, this zone of responsibility is not just left or right, east or west, but also north and south. So this is how you provide for the entirety of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before we complete this part of the examination, two more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Residovic, we haven't time for two more questions. We've run over by two to three minutes already.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must now adjourn. We resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of March, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
